implementation: Added host-bounded Taylor category 30/31 and archive retrieval using the observed archive controls, response size/run byte bounds, contiguous ranges, stable totals, terminal disabled control, unique article/arcId identities, and repeated first-page total/identity check.

Preserved article ID and arcId as separate observation identity; raw article hashes and category/archive response hashes are attached to evidence extraction metadata. Archive table Published Date and Archived Date are kept as labeled excerpt metadata; event_date remains UNKNOWN unless separately supported.

Selects the visible CivicPlus main h1.article-header-title and article-content body; a generic News Flash heading or missing content fails closed. The retained official Project Comal article 2032 now produces a planning Signal from its own sentence linking a data center to address 1051 CR 401, with Taylor, Texas supplied by the configured official source geography. The page footer is excluded from title/body interpretation.
Planning Signals include no MW, load, supply, buyer, cancellation, Prospect, or Lead claim. Withdrawn records are rejected by the interpreter and retained as observations/evidence.

The archive interval now ends on the retrieval date and spans a configured 59-day window plus seven-day overlap. Tests inject the cutoff date. Registry entry remains disabled pending controller runtime acceptance.

Explicit News category crossposts linked from category 30/31 are retained as non-target observations; complete category retrieval continues, while missing/unknown categories remain fail-closed and the Taylor interpreter cannot create a Signal for News.

Withdrawn archive revisions are linked to an existing Taylor Signal only through exact same-source numeric article identity and exactly one earlier accepted same-article Signal need. The retained withdrawn evidence is attached to that need with UNKNOWN status/reason; no lifecycle event, cancellation, new need, or power/supply fact is created. Missing or ambiguous matching remains unlinked with reason UNKNOWN.

Changed category extraction to require exactly one nonempty article-header .article-badge, excluding the related-news footer and reading the posted date separately. Exact category labels are preserved without fuzzy matching; only Development News and Development Notices pass the existing Taylor planning interpreter.

Archive row totals, page ranges, and article/arcId identity checks run across the complete mixed-category listing before article parsing/filtering. Every bounded revision is retained as a record with exact category, article source hash, archive dates, and archive page/category evidence hashes, including News and unrelated categories; no Signal/lifecycle/project link is created from those non-target rows.

Replaced unbounded hash concatenation in Evidence.extraction_location with a meaningful bounded locator containing the exact category badge; archive locators also identify table dates. The locator is length-checked against the existing varchar(100) limit and fails explicitly instead of truncating. Article/revision identity, URL, full-response source hash, and separately labeled archive dates remain in their existing record/evidence fields.

Category-root and archive-page response hashes are not individually copied into database evidence rows. The approved raw upstream page captures and recorded hashes remain available in the retained GL3-015B access artifacts and ACCESS.json for inspection/replay.

Taylor Project identity is now keyed by the numeric article ID, while observation/evidence identity retains each arcId. A later accepted revision reuses the unique prior accepted Signal project/need. Conflicting project labels or distinct article site addresses, or multiple prior projects for one article, cause a retained UNKNOWN observation with no new Signal/project link/lifecycle effect. Different numeric article IDs remain distinct absent the existing independent physical-site plus project-name matcher evidence.

Publication date parsing is limited to the article category header and head publication metadata. The whole-page MM/DD/YYYY fallback was removed, so dates in body/related/footer content cannot satisfy dated Signal admission; absence or malformed publication date fails closed.

For in-place changes to a Taylor category-page observation, the identity guard now compares the incoming record against all retained Evidence for the same numeric article, including prior Evidence attached to the currently changing external ID, as well as prior archive revisions. Explicit conflicting project labels or site addresses leave the new version as UNKNOWN before Project rename, Signal acceptance, or lifecycle advancement.

The prior accepted interpretation assessment is retained in the changed version assessment history when identity is UNKNOWN. Raw Observation and new Evidence remain stored, while the existing Project name, Signal need, and lifecycle history stay unchanged.
